problem: Which of the following **cannot** be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x)?$
worked_solution:
Notice that we are given an equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x).
$$

The right-hand side is a function of $x$ only. This means that, for a fixed value of $x,$ the slope field does not vary with $y.$ 

Of the given slope fields, the only one that varies with $y$ for a fixed value of $x$ is the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040080/assets/e00df97d8362b857f927d3c572cf09a6e442ff1af639e7cfccaffdded5c4924d.png)

 

To see this more clearly, notice that if we draw a vertical line, the slopes touching the line vary as we go up and down the line. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040080/assets/42e282935d15a2d48c07a25e5cb29be405ce9705add2a8cd4d98671dd5427516.png)
